topics.title: What is ShareBite?
topics.body: ShareBite (Bite Sharing) is a zero-food-waste donation platform: hotels and donors list surplus meals, NGOs and needy users request them, volunteers pick up and deliver (or route to compost), and compost agencies complete organic disposal. Everyone has a role-specific dashboard after login.

topics.title: Login and registration
topics.body: Use **Register** to choose your role (Hotel, NGO, Needy, Volunteer, Compost agency) and submit details. An **Admin** may need to **approve** you before you can use protected features. Use **Login** with username and password; you receive a **JWT token** stored in the browser. After login you are redirected to the correct dashboard for your role.

topics.title: Account pending or not approved
topics.body: New accounts can be in **PENDING** until an Admin approves them. If you see warnings or cannot upload, your account may still be pending. Contact your organization’s admin or the system administrator. Admins use the Admin panel to review users.

topics.title: Session and token issues
topics.body: The app stores your **token** after login. If it **expires** or is invalid, you may get **401** and be sent to login again. Try **logging out and back in**. Ensure the frontend `api.js` **base URL** matches your Spring server. Do not share your token.

topics.title: User roles on ShareBite
topics.body: **HOTEL** — list surplus food donations. **NEEDY** — browse and request meals. **VOLUNTEER** — accept pickups, deliver, live tracking. **NGO** — coordinate distribution. **COMPOST_AGENCY** — handle spoiled/organic waste with proof. **ADMIN** — approve users and oversee the system. Each role opens a different URL after login (`/hotel`, `/needy`, etc.).

topics.title: Publishing a donation (Hotel)
topics.body: Click **Publish donation**. Fill **food name**, **description**, **quantity**, **expiry date/time**, **donation type**, **pickup address**, optional **latitude/longitude**, and optional **photo**. Submit saves the donation as **PENDING** so others can request it. You earn **gamification points** for creating donations.

topics.title: Donation types: Human, Dog, Compost
topics.body: **HUMAN** — food safe for people. **DOG** — suitable for stray dogs. **COMPOST** — not for eating; goes to composting / organic processing. Choose the type when publishing; needy users filter **available** donations by type. AI may suggest **COMPOST** if a photo looks unsafe for humans.

topics.title: Donation status lifecycle
topics.body: Typical flow: **PENDING** (listed) → **ACCEPTED** (someone took the request) → **PICKED_UP** → **DELIVERED** or **COMPOSTED**. **EXPIRED** if the meal passes its expiry while still pending. Hotels see status in their donation table; volunteers update progress.

topics.title: Expiry date on donations
topics.body: Every donation has an **expiry date/time** you set. The system can **mark donations expired** when that time passes. The **AI suggested expiry** (e.g. a few hours for confident fresh food) only fills the field if it was empty and auto-assist is on — you can always edit it.

topics.title: Food photos and uploads
topics.body: Choose an **image** on the donation form; the app uploads it to Spring (`/api/files/upload`) and stores a **photo URL** on the donation. **Images only**; large files may hit the **10MB** multipart limit in `application.properties`. On phones, picking from gallery or camera both produce a file upload — same flow.

topics.title: AI food freshness (Hotel)
topics.body: **Smart food assessment** sends your photo through Spring (`/api/freshness/ml/predict`) to a **Python FastAPI** service running a **TensorFlow/Keras** model. With **auto-assist** on, analysis runs automatically after you pick a photo (debounced). Results: **FRESH / ROTTEN**, confidence, message, suggested hours. **Train** the model from `freshness-api` with `download_dataset.py` and `train.py` to produce `food_model.h5`.

topics.title: Configuring the AI service
topics.body: In Spring `application.properties`, set **freshness.api.base-url** to your Python host (e.g. `http://localhost:8000`). Run from `freshness-api`: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, optionally `python download_dataset.py`, `python train.py`, then `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`. If the model is missing, `/predict` returns **503** — check `/health` on the Python app.

topics.title: AI freshness vs star ratings
topics.body: **Hotel AI** — automated image classifier before or at donation time (CNN). **Needy star ratings** — after delivery, recipients rate **1–5** freshness manually via `/api/freshness`. They measure different things; both can coexist for trust and feedback.

topics.title: Needy: browsing and requesting
topics.body: Open the **Needy** dashboard. Browse **available donations** by type (human/dog/compost where applicable). Create a **request** tied to a donation; track request **status**. After delivery you can leave a **freshness star rating** and comment for that donation.

topics.title: Volunteer pickups and delivery
topics.body: Volunteers see **requests** for donations (often from needy users). **Accept** or progress the assignment, update **status**, and use **live location** so the hotel donor can **track** the route on the map (WebSocket + OpenStreetMap). Upload **delivery proof** or **compost proof** when the workflow requires it.

topics.title: Live map tracking
topics.body: Hotels can **track** an active volunteer request on a **map** (e.g. Leaflet tiles). Updates come over **WebSocket** (`/ws`) from the backend. If the map is empty, the volunteer may not have started sharing location yet. **ETA** and distance may show when routing data is available.

topics.title: NGO panel
topics.body: NGOs use their dashboard to **review donations and requests** aligned with their mission — connecting surplus food to people in need. Features depend on your build; use lists and filters to find **pending** or **available** items.

topics.title: Compost agency
topics.body: Compost partners finalize items marked for **compost** disposal. Mark requests **COMPOSTED**, attach **compost proof** (photo/URL) and notes where the app asks. Hotels can see **compost proof** in tracking dialogs when status is composted.

topics.title: Admin panel
topics.body: **ADMIN** users open `/admin` to **approve pending registrations**, oversee users and activity, and keep the platform healthy. Default demo admin may exist in seed data — change passwords in production.

topics.title: Points, badges, and levels
topics.body: Users earn **points** for actions (e.g. creating donations, completing deliveries, compost events). The app shows **total points** and **level** on dashboards like the Hotel panel. **Badges** may be awarded for milestones. Details come from `/api/gamification` endpoints.

topics.title: Database (MySQL)
topics.body: Spring Boot uses **MySQL** (`spring.datasource.url` in `application.properties`, database name often **bitesharing**). Ensure MySQL is running, credentials match, and `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update` for dev. **503 / DATABASE_ERROR** usually means the API cannot reach the database — fix host, port **3306**, user, password, or firewall.

topics.title: Frontend API base URL
topics.body: React’s `src/utils/api.js` sets **API_BASE_URL** (e.g. `http://localhost:8080/api` or your LAN IP). It must match where **Spring Boot** listens. **CORS** in Spring allows origins like `http://localhost:3000`. If calls fail, verify URL, that Spring is up, and browser console for CORS or mixed-content errors.

topics.title: This help assistant
topics.body: Answers come from a **built-in JSON knowledge base** on the server plus optional **Ollama** (local LLM) when enabled in `application.properties`. To improve answers, edit **`chatbot/knowledge.json`** and restart Spring. For smarter paraphrases, install Ollama and set **chatbot.ollama.enabled=true**.

topics.title: Dark mode
topics.body: Dashboards with a **theme toggle** (moon/sun icon) switch **dark** and **light** mode for comfort. Preference is typically in React state from the parent `App` component.

topics.title: Donations for stray dogs
topics.body: When publishing, choose donation type **DOG** (Stray dogs) if food is meant for animals, not human consumption. Needy/stray workflows can filter by type. Do not list unsafe human food as HUMAN.

topics.title: Delivery and compost proof
topics.body: Volunteers or agencies may upload **proof images** when a delivery or compost run completes so donors and admins can verify outcomes. Look for proof sections in tracking or request dialogs.

topics.title: Real-time updates
topics.body: Some features use **WebSockets** (e.g. SockJS/STOMP to `/ws`) for live tracking. If live updates fail, confirm Spring WebSocket config and that nothing blocks WebSocket on your network or reverse proxy.

topics.title: Training the freshness model
topics.body: From **`freshness-api`**: run **`python download_dataset.py`** to pull a large fruit fresh/rotten set (Hugging Face), then **`python train.py`** to produce **`food_model.h5`** and **`class_indices.json`**. Add your own photos under `dataset/train` and `validation` folders to improve domain coverage. See **`RUN.txt`** in that folder.

topics.title: Uncertain AI results
topics.body: If confidence is **below ~0.6**, the model shows an **uncertain** style message and conservative handling. Treat AI as **assistive**, not a legal food-safety certificate — use human judgment and local regulations.

topics.title: Spring Boot server port
topics.body: Default API port is often **8080** (`server.port` in `application.properties`). The React app must point to the same host/port in `api.js`. Python freshness usually uses **8000** — different port, configured separately.

topics.title: JWT configuration
topics.body: **jwt.secret** and **jwt.expiration** in `application.properties` control token signing and lifetime. Use a **long random secret** in production. After changing secrets, all users must **log in again**.

topics.title: Where files are stored
topics.body: Uploaded images are saved under **`file.upload.dir`** (default `./uploads` relative to Spring’s working directory). Ensure that folder is writable and backed up if you need durability.

topics.title: Maps API key
topics.body: If your build uses **Google Maps**, set **`google.maps.api.key`** in `application.properties`. OpenStreetMap tiles may be used elsewhere without that key — depends on component.

topics.title: SMS configuration
topics.body: Placeholders exist for **SMS API** keys in `application.properties` (`sms.api.key`, `sms.api.secret`). Wire them to your provider (e.g. Twilio) in code if SMS features are implemented in your branch.

topics.title: Production deployment tips
topics.body: Run Spring behind **HTTPS** (e.g. nginx), set strong **secrets**, restrict **MySQL** and **Python** services to internal networks, update **CORS** allowed origins to your real frontend domain, and use environment-specific `application.properties` or profiles.

topics.title: Points when creating a donation
topics.body: Creating a donation typically **awards points** (e.g. +10 in the default gamification hook) so donors stay motivated. Check your points card on the Hotel dashboard after publishing.

topics.title: Who creates pickup requests?
topics.body: **Needy** (or similar) users create **requests** against published donations. **Volunteers** fulfill pickups and updates. Hotels see **requests for their donations** in their dashboard sections (e.g. live request tracking).

topics.title: Quantity field
topics.body: **Quantity** is the number of **meals or portions** you are offering (integer). Be realistic so pickup and demand stay aligned.

topics.title: Pickup address and coordinates
topics.body: Enter a clear **pickup address** for volunteers. **Latitude/longitude** are optional but help maps and routing; you can paste coordinates if you have them.

topics.title: Image upload errors
topics.body: Upload requires **authentication** for `/api/files/upload`. The browser must send **multipart/form-data** with the file field; the React interceptor removes manual Content-Type so the boundary is correct. If **403**, your account may be **pending approval**.

topics.title: Ollama for the help chatbot
topics.body: Optional: set **chatbot.ollama.enabled=true**, **chatbot.ollama.base-url**, and **chatbot.ollama.model** in Spring. Install **Ollama** locally and `ollama pull` your model. The assistant uses it when FAQ match is weak — no cloud API key required.

topics.title: Privacy and data
topics.body: Donations and requests contain operational data (food details, locations, photos). Run ShareBite under your organization’s **privacy policy**; restrict admin access; use HTTPS in production; limit who can export database backups.

topics.title: AI service 503 or unavailable
topics.body: Start **uvicorn** for `freshness-api`, ensure **`food_model.h5`** exists after training, and verify **freshness.api.base-url** in Spring matches the Python host/port. Open **`GET /health`** on the Python app to see **model_loaded**.

topics.title: Refreshing data on dashboards
topics.body: Many panels have a **Refresh** button to reload donations or requests from the API. If lists look stale, click Refresh or re-open the page after ensuring Spring and MySQL are healthy.

topics.title: Zero food waste mission
topics.body: ShareBite aligns with **reducing food waste** and **feeding people** (or animals / compost) instead of landfills. Hotels reduce disposal costs; communities gain meals; volunteers earn recognition.

topics.title: Human support
topics.body: This assistant answers common **product** questions. For account bans, legal issues, or bugs not covered here, contact your **organization’s administrator** or the **development team** maintaining this deployment.

topics.title: Something is broken
topics.body: Check **browser devtools** (Network/Console) for failed API calls. Verify **Spring logs**, **MySQL** connectivity, and **Python** logs for AI. Note the **URL**, **HTTP status**, and steps to reproduce when reporting to developers.

topics.title: When to choose compost type
topics.body: If food is **spoiled** or **unsafe for humans**, use type **COMPOST** (or follow AI suggestion when confident). Human consumption donations must be **safe and within expiry**; never list clearly hazardous food as HUMAN.

topics.title: Home page statistics
topics.body: The marketing **home** page may show aggregate **stats** (donations, meals, volunteers) loaded from public or authenticated API endpoints depending on build — useful for impact storytelling.

topics.title: Volunteer points
topics.body: Completing deliveries or compost flows may **award points** (see gamification service rules in the backend). Check the Volunteer panel for your score.

topics.title: Hotel donation table
topics.body: The **donation history** table shows food, **donation type**, an **AI** chip if an ML prediction was stored, **quantity**, **expiry**, and **status**. Use it to audit what you published.

topics.title: Choosing a role at registration
topics.body: Pick the role that matches how you will use ShareBite: **Hotel** for surplus listings, **Needy** to request food, **Volunteer** for logistics, **NGO** for coordination, **Compost agency** for waste processing, **Admin** only if you operate the platform.

topics.title: Logging out
topics.body: Use **Logout** in the panel header to clear **token** and user info from the browser and return to the login screen. Use this on shared computers.

topics.title: Common API areas
topics.body: Spring exposes REST under **`/api`** — e.g. **donations**, **requests**, **files/upload**, **auth**, **gamification**, **freshness** (manual ratings), **freshness/ml/predict** (AI image), **chatbot**, **tracking**, **ws** for WebSocket. Explore controllers in the `backend` source for the full set.

topics.title: CORS errors
topics.body: If the browser blocks requests, add your frontend origin to Spring **CORS** config (`cors.allowed.origins` or `SecurityConfig`). Frontend and API **ports** must match what you configured (e.g. localhost:3000 → localhost:8080).

topics.title: Times and time zones
topics.body: Use consistent **time zones** for expiry fields. JDBC often uses **UTC** in URLs (`serverTimezone=UTC`). Pickup times should be clear to volunteers in **local** context.

topics.title: Server-side AI when publishing
topics.body: When a hotel **publishes** a donation with a photo stored under `/api/files/...`, Spring **reads that file** and calls the Python CNN again. **`mlFreshness*`** on the saved row comes from the **server**, not the browser. If AI says **ROTTEN** with high confidence and type is **HUMAN** or **DOG**, publish is **blocked** until you choose **COMPOST** or provide **`mlPolicyOverrideReason`** (15+ characters) for audit. Set **`freshness.publish.require-successful-ml=true`** to require AI to succeed whenever a local photo exists.

topics.title: Finding your way in the app
topics.body: After login you land on **your role’s dashboard**. Use page titles, **Publish donation** (Hotel), tables, and **Refresh**. The floating **Help** button opens this assistant on any supported screen.
